full_page.content:
1925, November
FR. SOLANUS, NOTEBOOK NO. 1.
Page 28 Cont.
Saturday, 9th 11 A.M. quiet after restless night and morning - about 8 convulsions. At. 12 Sleeps, 12.30 much improved - seemingly asleep, but smiles at remarks of Fr. S. to nurse. Then, seeing her conscious Fr. S. whispers: "That is right Veronica. Keep smiling and God bless you . .. in your better moments ask Jesus to strengthen you in resig- nation to this cross." She whispers the answer, nodding with a little smile, "I do ask Him."
November 10th four convulsions - restless.
November 11 saw her To-night - bright and cheerful. Parents wonder what to do - send her for sergical treatment or wait.
Nov. 18 Thursday (This A.M. I found the book. "Living Sisters ... " and to-night Mr. Rose reports, "Best day in two months ... Veronica came downstairs and was able to see."
Nov. 21st "Convulsions last night again ... and one this morning." - Yesterday I neglected my reading.
Dec. 2 "yesterday and To-day she is better & brighter ... preparing by novena for Feast of Our Bl. Mother - 8th
Dec. 22nd 23rd 24th Convulsions.
25th bright and happy.
26th worse again.
29 Convulsions - unconscious Her Father phones at 8 p.m. he fears she'll die To-night. The St. Therese Chapel he built in memory of his same Daughter Veronica is to be blest January 2nd next Sunday. Will the daughter live! We hope
Dec 30th 5.20 a.m. Mrs. Rose phones: "Veronica is dying." at 5.55 a.m. she passes from time to Eternity . R. I.P. Fulfilling promises to read "Autob'y" if she were spared (Oct. 1st) have come to page 144. To read it if Rt. Rev. Bishop consent favorably to con- tinuation of Shrine, am up to page 178 0! what a change! Yesterday in convulsions and under hypadermics she was deformed and swolen, her head seemed ready to burst, and rash covered her face and neck - black and blue; To-day her fearful struggle is over and reposes in triumph as a beautiful child of fifteen. -- a joy to behold. Thanks be to God for her cross and for her evident victory.
